issues.legal_issue: An appeal challenging a decision on court fee is maintainable when the plaint was rejected for nonpayment of court fee and the resulting decision is appealable as a decree.
material_facts: The trial court rejected the plaint under Order 7, Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure because the plaintiffs did not pay the court fee it required.
The High Court reversed that decision, and the defendant appealed to the Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court had granted special leave, and the dispute involved the legal interpretation of the court-fee provision.
issues.conclusion: The preliminary objection that the appeal was incompetent had no merit.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, an order rejecting a plaint is a decree and is appealable. A second appeal under section 100 may also lie where the interpretation of the court-fee provision raises a question of law. Rathnavarmaraja v. Smt. Vimla concerned revision and does not bar an appeal in these circumstances; Vasu v. Chakki Mani was cited on the distinction. In any event, once special leave has been granted, the question whether an appeal lies does not arise.

rule.if: plaint_rejected_for_nonpayment and appeal_challenges_court_fee_decision and (rejection_appealable_as_decree or special_leave_granted)

predicates.plaint_rejected_for_nonpayment: The trial court rejected the plaint because the plaintiff did not pay the required court fee.
predicates.appeal_challenges_court_fee_decision: A party appealed a decision concerning the court fee payable in the suit.
predicates.rejection_appealable_as_decree: The court rejected the plaint, producing a decision treated as a decree for appeal purposes.
predicates.special_leave_granted: The Supreme Court granted special leave to appeal.

issues.definition: When a court-fee appeal challenges a decision following rejection of a plaint for nonpayment, the appeal is maintainable if that rejection is appealable as a decree or special leave has been granted.

issues.legal_issue: A suit seeking a declaration that a decree against a father does not bind his sons’ interests in joint family property includes consequential relief when the decree remains executable against those interests unless set aside.
material_facts: The plaintiffs, who were sons, claimed that the mortgaged property was joint Hindu family property and that their father had mortgaged it without consideration or family necessity.
The mortgagee obtained a decree against the father and sought to execute it by sale of the mortgaged property.

The sons sued for a declaration that the mortgage and decree were null and void and ineffective against them, but did not expressly seek to set aside the decree or an injunction against its execution.
The sons paid a fixed court fee, and the plaint was rejected after they did not pay the fee assessed by the trial court.
issues.conclusion: The declaration sought involved consequential relief: the sons were required to seek the setting aside of the decree or equivalent relief restraining its execution and pay ad valorem court fee under section 7(iv)(c) of the Court Fees Act. The High Court’s contrary decision was incorrect.
issues.legal_principle: Court fee is determined from the allegations and prayer in the plaint, but the court examines the substance of the relief rather than allowing the form or drafting of the prayer to control. A decree against the father as manager may bind the other members’ interests in joint family property and remain executable against them unless set aside. The consequential relief therefore attracts section 7(iv)(c) of the Court Fees Act; sections 8 and 9 of the Suits Valuation Act were also discussed. The Court relied on Zeb-ul-Nisa v. Din Mohammad, Prithvi Raj v. D. C. Ralli and Vinayakrao v. Mankunwar Bai.

predicates.civil_suit_seeks_declaration_against_fam: A claimant brings a civil suit seeking a declaration concerning a decree obtained against the manager of a family.
predicates.decree_obtained_against_manager: A creditor obtained a decree against the person managing family property.
predicates.claimant_seeks_to_protect_interest_in_jo: A claimant asks the court to protect the claimant’s asserted interest in property held as joint family property.

issues.definition: When a civil suit seeks a declaration against a decree obtained against a family manager to protect an interest in joint family property, consequential relief requiring ad valorem court fee is involved.

issues.legal_issue: A father managing a joint Hindu family may expose the joint family estate to execution for a debt he incurs, including a mortgage debt, if the debt is not for an immoral purpose, even when it was not incurred for legal necessity.
material_facts: The father, who was the manager of the family, mortgaged property that the sons claimed was joint Hindu family property.
The sons alleged that the mortgage was made without consideration and family necessity.
The Court addressed whether a mortgage debt incurred by a father-manager could expose the joint family estate to execution despite the absence of legal necessity.
issues.conclusion: A father-manager’s debt may expose the joint family estate to execution if it was not incurred for an immoral purpose; the absence of legal necessity does not by itself prevent that result, including for a mortgage debt.
issues.legal_principle: Under Hindu law, a father who manages a joint family may incur a debt that exposes the joint family estate to execution, provided the debt is not for an immoral purpose. This applies to a mortgage debt for which the father is personally liable, even if the mortgage was not for legal necessity or payment of an antecedent debt. The Court relied on Faqir Chand v. Harnam Kaur.

rule.if: joint_family_debt_case and father_manages_family and father_incurred_debt and not debt_for_immoral_purpose

predicates.joint_family_debt_case: The dispute concerns a debt incurred by a father managing a Hindu joint family and its effect on family property.
predicates.father_manages_family: The father manages the joint family and its property.
predicates.father_incurred_debt: The father incurred a debt for which a creditor seeks payment from family property.
predicates.debt_for_immoral_purpose: The debt was incurred for an immoral purpose.

issues.definition: If a father managing a joint family incurs a debt that was not for an immoral purpose, the joint family estate may be exposed to execution for that debt.
